graph.title: Rescue Helicopter
notes: The booklet builds ONE model (the helicopter) plus three minifigs and a stretcher. The earlier 'separate groups' were the minifigs and stretcher; they are now connected to the helicopter as shown on the box art: medic 1 rests in the cockpit seat area (contact m2-b51), medic 2 stands on the cabin floor by the door (contact n2-b8), the winch hook clips to the stretcher handle (w9-str2), and the rescued workman lies on the stretcher (contact f2-str1).
The booklet is pictorial; stud-to-stud contacts are inferred from the step images, so some joins are approximated (a part is joined to the main plate it rests on rather than every neighbour).

Port convention: catalogue/new brick types expose a single 'stud.1' / 'anti-stud.1' port standing for the whole stud grid, so stud joins use null ports. Named ports are kept only for specific one-off features (pins into holes, clips, hinges, wheel pins/rims/tires, minifig head/helmet/hat/visor/hand connections).
White minifig legs: the inventory lists them as '9327', which is not a valid part number; the catalogue's white minifig legs (lego-73200) are used instead for both medics.
The second medic head (4200908) has a socket-type neck, so its neck join to the torso uses null ports.

Element IDs come from the inventory pages (45-46). Where an inventory ID collided with a catalogue entry with a different description (e.g. 4222017, 4211051, 4211080, 4204624, 4259937, 4219913) the catalogue type was reused for the matching booklet part.

Some inventory pieces are not clearly placed in the steps and are omitted: 2x 4259422, 1x 4212517, 1x 4160866, 3x 4244366, 4x 4219913, 3x 302321, 1x 302026, 2x 243121, 1x 300401 and several spare 4210631/4211001.
Rotor blades are one repeat x4; each copy attaches to its own rotor arm ra1..ra4 via attach overrides (ra1:stud.1 -> ra2/3/4:stud.1).
Tail rotor attaches via a pin (4211807) into 4211568; the main rotor hub (247926) turns on the pin of 4211666 on the roof.

graph_initial.title: Rescue Helicopter
notes: The booklet is pictorial; exact stud-to-stud contacts are inferred from the step images, so many joins are approximated (e.g. a part is joined to the main plate it rests on rather than every neighbour).

Element IDs come from the inventory pages (45-46). Where an inventory ID collided with a catalogue entry that has a different description (e.g. 4222017, 4211051, 4211080, 4204624, 4259937, 4219913) the catalogue type was reused for the matching booklet part.

Some inventory pieces were not clearly placed in the steps and are omitted from the graph: 2x 4259422, 1x 4212517, 1x 4160866, 3 more 4244366, 4x 4219913, 3x 302321, 1x 302026, 2x 243121, 1x 300401, 2x 407001-based extras, 2x 4286466 duplicates and several 4210631/4211001 spares.
Parts shown with null ports (e.g. 366621 uses top.1/bottom; handle plates 4222017, clip-to-handle joins) reflect that the catalogue ports do not distinguish clip/bar ends.
Rotor blades are one repeat x4; each copy attaches to its own rotor arm ra1..ra4 via attach overrides. The template's first edge to ra1 is replaced for copies 2-4.

Minifigs: two medics (white torso 4291215, white legs 9327, blue helmet 4106305 + visor 4163306), one rescued workman with red hard hat. The cockpit/winch-side seating of figures is not part of the numbered steps so no edges to the helicopter are given. The stretcher (471401 + two 471501 handles) is a separate model.
The tail rotor is attached via a pin (4211807) into 4211568; the main rotor hub (247926) turns on the pin of 4211666 on the roof.
